content.text:
Finding submitted.

**Classification: deviation (critical, indemnity)**

**What the document does:** Section 12 is the sole indemnity provision. Section 12(b) gives us a TrueLink indemnity, but only for "any breach by TrueLink of this Agreement or any failure by TrueLink in the performance of any of its obligations or agreements hereunder" — no third-party IP infringement cover, no duty to defend, no claims procedure. Nothing else fills the gap: TrueLink's only warranties (Section 9) are Y2K, and p0076 disclaims everything else, so there is no non-infringement warranty to breach. By contrast, Section 12(a) imposes a very broad Client indemnity (any Client breach, Web Site/Client Content claims, third-party product/service injury). That fails the fallback's threshold element (Vendor IP indemnity), so it is redlined rather than accepted at fallback.

**Target chosen — preferred, not fallback:** the fallback would require importing a 3× annual-fees super-cap into an indemnity that is currently uncapped (the p0077 cap reaches only Sections 3, 4, 7 and 11), which would be a self-inflicted downgrade; the preferred route needs no cap language.

**Smallest complete change (validated, ok:true):**
1. New Section 12(c) inserted after p0075: TrueLink defends and indemnifies Client and its affiliates against third-party claims for (i) IP infringement/misappropriation by the Interface, Hosting Services or Support Services, (ii) TrueLink's breach of applicable law, (iii) TrueLink-caused unauthorised access to Client Content or Credit Data, and (iv) TrueLink's gross negligence or willful misconduct — with notice, control of defence and reasonable cooperation mechanics applied to indemnities under Section 12.
2. p0072 replaced so our indemnity is limited to Client Content we provide and our own violations of applicable law (removes ~230 words, adds ~27).
